problem_type: storyboard visible entry loses workspace mode projection
symptom: After restart, a visible storyboard plan card can be clicked while the URL remains step=create and the dedicated storyboard editor does not become the active reentry surface.
direct_cause: StoryboardPlanCard updates the shared workspaceMode store directly, while WorkbenchShell only wrote the step query when app-bar navigation or initial mount ran; direct card actions therefore left the URL projection stale during cold reentry. The journey runner also queried the first global storyboard card, which could belong to a hidden WorkspaceSlot even when body text made the card appear present.
class_root: Workspace mode had two unsynchronized projections: the store controlled mounted WorkspaceSlot visibility, but URL step remained an independent navigation hint. Direct visible workspace actions could not establish one canonical mode across render, URL, and restart boundaries.
affected_population: Users reopening a project and entering storyboard from a visible plan card
Any workspace action that calls setWorkspaceMode outside the app-bar callback
Cold restart and browser history paths that consume the step query
entry_points: WorkbenchShell workspaceMode and URL step projection
StoryboardWorkspace active slot and editor mount
internal_only_reason: Workspace mode and step query are internal Nomi navigation contracts.
invariants: Every workspaceMode store transition projects the same mode to the URL step query, including direct visible card actions.
The storyboard WorkspaceSlot is active whenever workspaceMode is storyboard and StoryboardPlanEditor reads the active document plan.
URL synchronization does not invent storyboard data or bypass the visible card/editor boundary.
Journey evidence scopes storyboard cards and editors to the active WorkspaceSlot and never treats hidden slots as visible user actions.
generality_proof: All workspace surfaces converge on WorkbenchShell's single workspaceMode store and WorkspaceSlot map; synchronizing the URL from that store covers app-bar, card, task-center, onboarding, and future direct mode setters.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Project the shared mode store into the step query for every direct or indirect workspace transition.
Render the dedicated editor from the active document's canonical storyboard plan when the storyboard slot is active.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The shared WorkbenchShell effect observes this store transition and writes step=storyboard.
The existing callback and new mode effect converge on the same URL writer.

recurrence.reason: Any future direct workspaceMode setter could otherwise leave URL navigation stale and reproduce the same reentry mismatch.
same_class_scan: Searched setWorkspaceMode callers across src/workbench and onboarding.
Confirmed WorkbenchShell is the only WorkspaceSlot/step projection owner.

prevention.invariant: URL step is derived from the shared workspaceMode store after every mode change.
prevention.failure_mode: Unknown mode values are rejected by the existing store setter; URL writer maps only the closed WorkspaceMode union.
prevention.strategy: Observe workspaceMode in one effect and reuse writeWorkspaceModeToUrl instead of adding caller-specific URL writes.

legacy_paths.rationale: The app-bar path remains; direct setters now share the same URL projection boundary.

migration: No persisted migration is needed; URL step is ephemeral navigation state.
residual_risks: A stale URL can still be observed for one render before the synchronization effect runs; the store remains the render authority.
If the active document plan is absent, the dedicated storyboard workspace continues to show its existing empty state.
